title: Hosted API Demo: Chat & Text Generation Basics - Orion Analytics
summary: AE + SE walked through Redwood hosted API chat and text generation fundamentals: streaming, key params (temperature/top_p/max_tokens), retry semantics, rate limits, and Console demo for observability. Customer concerned about latency, throughput, and security. Agreed to run a short latency benchmark and share security docs + pricing; SE to own benchmark. Next step: POC scoping call scheduled.
next_steps: Send hosted API pricing and quota sheet (Sophie)
Share SOC 2 and security whitepaper + KMS integration notes (Sophie)
Run latency/throughput benchmark with sample dataset, SE to coordinate (Daniel)
Schedule POC scoping call for next week to define success criteria (All)
Provide example streaming client snippet and retry pattern (Daniel)
action_items: Sophie: Send pricing & security artifacts by 2026-06-15
Priya: Share sample dataset and expected QPS by 2026-06-18
meeting_header: Date: 2026-06-14 | Time: 15:00 UTC | Duration: 45m | Attendees: Sophie Martin, Daniel Chu (Redwood)  Priya Patel, Marcus Reed, Aisha Khan (Orion Analytics)
transcript: 00:00 Sophie: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh this is Sophie from Redwood, i'm joined by Daniel our solutions engineer. how's everyone doing?
00:06 Priya: Doing well, thanks. we're excited to see the hosted API demo  we've been evaluating options for chat Gen for our analytics UI.

00:12 Sophie: Awesome; quick agenda: we'll run through the Hosted API for chat/text gen, streaming demo, go over key parameters like temperature/top_p/max_tokens, cover retries and rate limits, then demo the Console and Optimize tips. any additions?
00:22 Marcus: No, that's great. we care most about tail latency and cost per query  also, we have strict data residency and encryption needs so will want to see security docs later.
00:30 Daniel: got it. we'll call out latency vs cost tradeoffs and how batching / KV cache can help. quick question on QPS  what's target?
00:36 Priya: Right now proof-of-concept is 50 qps peak, expected production maybe 200 qps, and some requests are short context (few hundred tokens) others are long chat history ~2k tokens.

00:46 Daniel: good to know. Redwood hosted supports streaming responses so you can start rendering partial tokens as they arrive, and we tune batching to keep tail latency low  we'll demo streaming in a sec.
01:00 Sophie: i'll share the demo deck and a link to the hosted API quickstart in the chat  link: https://redwood.ai/docs/hosted-api
01:10 Aisha: quick note on security: do you support customer-managed keys / KMS?

01:14 Daniel: yes, we support KMS integrations for Private deployments and we have envelope encryption for hosted  i'll include the security whitepaper. for hosted we also have audit logs and SSO/SAML support.

02:00 Daniel: ok demo time  i'll switch screens, showing the simple curl/JS snippet. first example is a chat completion with streaming = true. code sends messages array, model selection from our catalog, and sample params: temperature 0.2, top_p 0.95, max_tokens 512.
02:20 Marcus: can you explain how retries work? we sometimes see transient 504s with other vendors.

02:25 Daniel: yes so our client libs have an idempotency and retry policy recommendations  for non-idempotent chat you should retry only on safe error classes; we expose Retry-After headers and an x-request-id to correlate. also we offer automatic client retry helpers in the SDK.
03:05 Priya: and streaming  does streaming increase cost?

03:10 Daniel: streaming itself doesn't increase token billing; billing is per-token output + input tokens. streaming reduces perceived latency because you get chunks earlier. watch out for chunk overhead on many tiny tokens but it's usually minimal.

04:00 Daniel: demoing the streaming client now  you can see partial outputs coming every 200ms in this example, and the Console shows per-request timing breakdown  start-to-first-byte, total tokens, model variant used.

04:30 Sophie: note on model catalog  we surface verified models with profile info (latency/cost) and variants for lower precision quantized options that are cheaper but slightly higher latency variance sometimes.
05:00 Marcus: what's the default concurrency / rate limit on hosted?

05:05 Sophie: default rate limits depend on plan; we'll send the quota table, but for demos we can provision a higher burst and support dedicated reserved capacity if you need steady 200 qps with SLA.
06:00 Priya: for long histories we worry about KV cache / context window. how does Redwood handle incremental chat with KV cache?

06:08 Daniel: our serving runtime manages KV cache per-session to avoid re-encoding repeated prefixes; that reduces compute for long chats. sometimes the transcription will call it K V caching which is a bit noisy in older docs, but functionally it's the token cache.
07:00 Aisha: any known issues with multi-tenant hosted and data isolation? we need assurance client data from one tenant isn't visible to others.
07:08 Sophie: hosted keeps customer data isolated logically and we have strict access controls, logging, and can do dedicated capacity for stronger isolation. we'll attach the SOC2 + ISO notes.

08:00 Daniel: switching back to the Console  here you can filter by route/model and see latency percentiles, token counts, and per-token cost breakouts. Optimize also surfaces batching suggestions and recommended model/quantization combos for your workload.
10:00 Marcus: about retries again  does Redwood guarantee ordering when streaming chunks with retries?

10:08 Daniel: good question. if a stream disconnects mid-response, the SDK will either retry from client-side with a new call or you can reconstruct using the conversation state; ordering is best-effort unless you use session-managed append semantics  we'll send detailed guidance.
12:00 Priya: what's our expected cost delta moving from our current provider? we need a rough t-shirt estimate.
12:10 Sophie: we'll run a quick cost comparison once you share sample traffic; Optimize gives estimated dollars per 1k tokens for different model variants which helps decisioning.

15:00 Daniel: a quick note on parameters  temperature controls randomness, top_p is nucleus sampling; for deterministic output set temperature 0 and top_p 1. Also use max_tokens to cap token usage. client-side you can also set stop sequences to avoid runaway output.
18:00 Marcus: any SDK examples for exponential backoff?
18:05 Daniel: yes, the JS/py SDKs have retries with jitter and we recommend starting with 500ms base and 2-3 retries for 5xx; avoid retrying on 4xx. we'll share snippet.

20:00 Sophie: ok recapping  we'll share pricing, security docs, and SDK snippets. Daniel will run a latency benchmark; Priya will share sample dataset and expected QPS. we'll schedule POC scoping next week.
20:30 Priya: thanks, that sounds good. one more small ask  can you show a quick example of streaming + partial UI rendering?
21:00 Daniel: yep i'll drop a small React snippet in the follow-up email; it hooks the streaming events into a DOM append so you don't block on full completion.
22:00 Aisha: timeline: if POC looks good we'd aim to start pilot in July and potentially move to dedicated reserved infra by Q4 if performance and security checks out.
23:00 Sophie: perfect  noted. i'll send calendar invite for the scoping call; thanks everyone for your time.
23:10 Marcus: thanks Sophie, Daniel. bye.
23:12 Priya: thanks, bye.
